evidence_quote: The target population for this study is comprised of students in second through fifth grades who are below grade level in reading or math, but not by more than two years. At the beginning of the study, local staff members ... were asked to identify students in need of supplemental academic support to meet local academic standards.
resolved_title: The Evaluation of Enhanced Academic Instruction in After-School Programs: Final Report. NCEE 2009-4077
notes: Kraft row is the math (Mathletics) after-school sample, grades 2-5. Students were drawn from after-school enrollees, identified by staff as below grade level, and parents had to consent and apply before the lottery, so opt_in = 1. Students with serious learning disabilities or behavior problems were excluded.

evidence_quote: This study targeted middle schools in districts in Southern California in which English language learner students classified as limited English proficient comprised at least 10 percent of the student population.
resolved_title: Evaluation of Quality Teaching for English Learners (QTEL) Professional Development. Final Report. NCEE 2012-4005
notes: School-level selection on English learner concentration (at least 10 percent LEP). Kraft's reading effects (CST-ELA, grades 7-8, n about 8,100 to 18,200) are for all students of exposed teachers, not only English learners; the CELDT sample is LEP students only but is not in Kraft's row.

resolved_title: The Impact of the Measures of Academic Progress (MAP) Program on Student Reading Achievement. Final Report. NCEE 2013-4000
notes: Illinois schools eligible only if new to MAP; all grade 4 and 5 students of regular classroom teachers. No need-based rule. The wwc-codes.csv row for 197 is matched to Smith, Cobb, Farran, Cordray, and Munter (2013), a math tutoring study, not this MAP report; that WWC match looks wrong.

evidence_quote: The study examined the impact of the Pathway Project intervention on students who were mainstreamed Latino English language learners (ELLs). One hundred and three English teachers in 15 schools in California were recruited and randomly assigned
resolved_title: WWC Review of the Report: A Randomized Experiment of a Cognitive Strategies Approach to Text-Based Analytical Writing for Mainstreamed Latino English Language Learners in Grades 6 to 12

evidence_quote: To be eligible to participate, schools had to be part of the NYCDOE public school system and have an existing arts program in at least one arts discipline. ... resolved_title: Scaling up the Success for All Model of School Reform: Final Report from the Investing in Innovation (i3) Evaluation
notes: School-level poverty criterion (at least 40 percent FRL) set by the program's own eligibility rule; within schools, all kindergarten students in regular classes were included (p. 14 to 15). Kraft's n 1,625 to 1,659 matches the kindergarten cohort followed to grade 2.

evidence_quote: Sixty-seven schools from 32 districts in Colorado participated in the study. These schools were not specifically selected using any sampling methodology; rather, they volunteered to participate in the study.
resolved_title: Classroom Assessment for Student Learning: Impact on Elementary School Mathematics in the Central Region. Final Report. NCEE 2011-4005
notes: Volunteer Colorado elementary schools randomized; all grade 4 and 5 students in study schools. No need-based rule (tie-breaker 6).

evidence_quote: So1 personnel also endeavored to select schools with a strong need for the program, giving preference to schools serving greater percentages of students eligible for Title I, English as a Second Language (ESL), and special education services.
resolved_title: Evaluation Report on the School of One i3 Expansion
notes: Borderline. Eight volunteer NYC middle schools were chosen from applicants with a stated preference for high-need (Title I, ESL, special education) schools, then schools or academies were randomized within pairs; all enrolled students are in the analysis sample (p. 9). Coded targeted_other at the school level because need was an explicit selection preference; a reviewer could argue universal since it was a preference, not a rule.

Kraft's n = 275 and grades 3-4 match the table row; Kraft's three effects (0.40, 0.28, 0.37) are not all in the table, which lists only +0.37.

evidence_quote: First, we implement the lottery-based design described above in sufficiently oversubscribed KIPP middle schools. ... evidence_quote: All schools that expressed interest in participating in the study were determined to be at least minimally ready to implement ANet; none were screened out. ... Within each school in the samples described above, all students in Grades 3 through 8 with either a nonmissing math or reading test score are included in the Year 2 analyses.
resolved_title: Achievement Network's Investing in Innovation Expansion: Impacts on Educator Practice and Student Achievement
notes: Schools in five districts volunteered in exchange for subsidized ANet services; a readiness screener excluded no one; all grade 3 to 8 students. The report notes the recruited schools served high shares of low-income students but states no such criterion. Kraft's n 13,233 (grades 3-5) and 21,335 (all) match the report. The wwc-codes.csv row for 986 is matched to Snipes et al. (2015), a summer math study, which is the wrong WWC review.

evidence_quote: Students became eligible for the study when they applied to a participating charter school at the school's entry grade. However, only students who applied during the school's primary application period and participated in the school's admissions lottery were included in the evaluation sample.
resolved_title: The Evaluation of Charter School Impacts: Final Report. NCEE 2010-4029
notes: Lottery applicants to 36 oversubscribed charter middle schools; opt_in = 1. Schools had to be oversubscribed and serve middle grades, with no need-based criterion; the report notes the study schools served relatively advantaged students.

evidence_quote: To be eligible to participate in the study, an elementary school had to serve students in grades 2-5, to have not implemented LIC in the past, and to have at least half of all teachers of grades 2-5 in each grade agree to participate. All traditional teachers of grades 2-5 and their students were eligible to participate.
resolved_title: Lessons in Character Impact Evaluation. Final Report. NCEE 2012-4004
notes: Fifty volunteer California elementary schools recruited by mass mailing; primary analytic sample is all grade 4 and 5 students in traditional classrooms. No need-based rule (tie-breaker 6).

evidence_quote: The study's target population was low- to moderate-performing public elementary schools ... Low- to moderate-performing schools were defined as schools that did not make adequate yearly progress (AYP) for any of the three school years prior to the 2008/09 school year or that were at risk of not making AYP.
resolved_title: A Study of the Effectiveness of a School Improvement Intervention (Success in Sight). Final Report. NCEE 2012-4014
notes: School-level selection on performance (missed AYP in any of three prior years, or at risk of missing it per school staff); all grade 3 to 5 students in the 52 Minnesota and Missouri schools. The wwc-codes.csv row for 1071 is matched to Ukrainetz et al. (2011), a preschool phonemic awareness study, which is the wrong WWC review.

evidence_quote: The purpose of the new scholarship program was to provide low-income residents, particularly those whose children attend schools in need of improvement (SINI) or corrective action under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, with “expanded opportunities to attend higher performing schools in the District of Columbia”
evidence_location: p. 1 (PDF p. 17); income cutoff of 185 percent of poverty on PDF p. 34
resolved_title: Evaluation of the DC Opportunity Scholarship Program: Final Report. NCEE 2010-4018
notes: Sample is 2,308 income-eligible applicants (family income at or below 185 percent of the federal poverty line) entered in scholarship lotteries in cohorts 1 and 2; Kraft's n = 2,300 matches. Individual income eligibility plus application makes this targeted_other with opt_in = 1. Lottery priority went to students from SINI schools (a school-performance criterion), but SINI status was a priority rule, not an eligibility rule; SINI subgroup effects are reported separately and are not Kraft's row.

evidence_quote: We use high-quality data from a large-scale school-level cluster randomized experiment to examine the impact of two well-known commercial interim assessment programs on mathematics and reading achievement in Indiana.
resolved_title: The Impact of Indiana's System of Interim Assessments on Mathematics and Reading Achievement
notes: Abstract only (Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis, paywalled); it names the design and state but no school or student eligibility rule, and no WWC sample text exists for this study. Kraft's n 11,623 to 20,000 could not be checked.

evidence_quote: This evaluation included 60 high-poverty rural schools across Missouri that were randomly assigned to two treatment conditions and a control condition, with approximately 200 teachers and 3,000 students in the 2011-2012 baseline academic year.
resolved_title: Impact Results of the eMINTS Professional Development Validation Study
notes: Abstract only. The abstract describes the sample as high-poverty rural schools but does not say whether schools were selected on poverty or rurality, so per the codebook this is unclear rather than a guess; if the full report confirms a poverty or rural eligibility rule for the i3 validation grant, the code becomes targeted_other with level = school. Kraft's n 1,931 to 3,295 is consistent with the 3,000 baseline students.

evidence_quote: Teachers taught multiple sections of ELA or reading; sections were randomly assigned to a treatment or comparison condition, and any extra classes were assigned to the treatment condition. There were 26 CSR and 22 comparison classes.
resolved_title: Collaborative Strategic Reading: Findings From Experienced Implementers (Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 2013)
notes: recoded after re-retrieval 2026-09-18: the abstract (ERIC EJ998840, DOI 10.1080/19345747.2012.741661) is Vaughn, Roberts, Klingner, Swanson, Boardman, Stillman-Spisak, Mohammed, and Leroux 2013, the CSR experienced-implementer trial that carries Kraft's n_max 472 and three of the four effects. Whole English/Language Arts or Reading class sections of 12 teachers in Texas and Colorado middle schools were randomized; no student-level rule is stated. The Reading sections might be remedial classes, but the abstract does not say so, hence medium. mixed_samples 1 because Kraft's study 954 also folds in one Fryer row (n 419, grade 8, GMRT 0.195) from a different trial, Vaughn, Swanson, Roberts, Wanzek, Stillman-Spisak, Solis, and Simmons 2013, Reading Research Quarterly 48(1). Neither article has an open full text.

evidence_quote: Classrooms were randomly assigned to within-school experimental and control groups. Participating students were pre- and post-tested using two standardized, nationally normed tests of math achievement.
resolved_title: Effect of Technology-Enhanced Continuous Progress Monitoring on Math Achievement
notes: Abstract only (School Psychology Review, paywalled); no eligibility rule stated. The wwc-codes.csv row for 1030 is the WWC review of Ysseldyke and Tardrew (2007), a related Accelerated Math paper; its sample text (47 schools in 24 states, grades 3-6, 17 percent FRL) gives demographics only, so it does not settle the code either. Kraft's n 823 to 1,880 could not be checked.

evidence_quote: districts had to meet criteria for size, poverty, and need for induction: at least 570 teachers in elementary schools, at least 10 elementary schools with 50 percent or more students eligible for free or reduced-price meals under the federal National School Lunch Program, and no existing comprehensive induction program offered in study schools.
evidence_location: PDF p. 26, Executive Summary, Study Design (printed p. xxv)
resolved_title: Impacts of Comprehensive Teacher Induction: Final Results from a Randomized Controlled Study (NCEE 2010-4027, June 2010)
notes: recoded after re-retrieval 2026-09-18: first page names Glazerman, Isenberg, Dolfin, Bleeker, Johnson, Grider, and Jacobus (Mathematica, NCEE 2010-4027, June 2010), the report Kraft's ies90 row cites. Seventeen districts in 13 states were chosen from 98 that met size and poverty targets; within districts, all or a district-chosen subset of elementary schools with eligible beginning teachers (new to the profession, grades K-6) were randomized, and the students of those teachers form the test-score sample. Coded targeted_other at the school level because the poverty criterion (at least 10 schools with 50 percent or more NSLP) was part of district selection. Confidence medium rather than high because the criterion operated on the district pool, not on each study school (study schools averaged about 59 percent NSLP, Table II), so a reviewer could read the sample as universal. Kraft's grade 4 rows (n 614 and 741) are the by-grade test-score subsamples of the K-6 sample.
